macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks slip as investors await CPI
items.summary: Major U.S. indexes ended lower ahead of Wednesday’s September CPI report, with the Nasdaq 100 reaching a 1.5-week low. Inflation expectations and uncertainty over possible Federal Reserve rate hikes kept risk appetite subdued.[1]

items.title: Markets brace for inflation data and Fed Beige Book
items.summary: Investors are focused on September CPI data, expected to show annual inflation accelerating to 3.6%, and the Federal Reserve’s Beige Book. New York Fed President John Williams said another rate increase could be appropriate this year while signaling less urgency for additional hikes in 2027.[2]

items.title: U.S. stock futures edge higher before CPI and bank earnings
items.summary: Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq futures moved modestly higher in premarket trading as investors awaited inflation data and results from Bank of America, Morgan Stanley, and BlackRock. A hotter-than-expected CPI reading could revive expectations for an October Fed rate hike.[3]

items.title: Bank earnings provide mixed signals
items.summary: JPMorgan, Citigroup, and Wells Fargo reported strong lending-related earnings, but market reactions were mixed. Wells Fargo faced pressure after reporting weaker-than-expected net interest income, while broader bank results failed to lift equities.[4]

items.title: ASML raises annual outlook again
items.summary: Dutch semiconductor-equipment maker ASML raised its annual forecast for the third time this year, citing strong demand for equipment used to build artificial-intelligence chips and efforts to expand output.[5]

items.title: China export growth beats forecasts
items.summary: China’s exports grew faster than expected in September, supported by robust overseas demand that helped offset weak domestic consumer spending.[2]

items.title: Applied Materials and Domino’s shares fall
items.summary: Applied Materials dropped after providing limited detail on its outlook at an investor event, while Domino’s declined after reporting domestic comparable-store sales growth below analyst expectations.[1]

items.title: Meta gains on new AI model announcement
items.summary: Meta Platforms shares rose after the company announced Muse Wonder, a new artificial-intelligence model that it described as having advanced capabilities.[1]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin falls below $83,000 as crypto markets weaken
items.summary: Bitcoin dropped below $83,000, while ether fell below $2,500. U.S. spot Bitcoin and ether ETFs also recorded sizable net outflows, signaling continued risk-off sentiment.[5][8]

items.title: Meteora launches DLMM Pro as MET token surges
items.summary: Solana-based DeFi protocol Meteora announced DLMM Pro, sending its MET token up 44.6% over 24 hours, according to market data cited by Odaily.[5]

items.title: CFTC outlines proposed crypto-market regulatory framework
items.summary: CFTC Chair Mike Selig said the agency’s proposed framework is intended to establish federal oversight and protect exchange customers from fraud, market manipulation and loss of customer funds.[8]

items.title: South Korea blocks websites of unregistered crypto exchanges
items.summary: South Korean authorities reportedly blocked access to KuCoin, MEXC and 25 other unregistered exchanges, urging users to withdraw their assets from the platforms.[7]

items.title: Blockchain.com seeks U.S. licenses for prediction markets and derivatives
items.summary: Blockchain.com has applied to the CFTC for licenses that would allow it to offer prediction markets and crypto derivatives to U.S. retail and institutional customers.[1][9]

items.title: EU regulators set deadline for crypto firms to exit non-compliant stablecoins
items.summary: ESMA said MiCA-authorized crypto firms must clear remaining exposure to non-compliant stablecoins by January 8, 2027, affecting services involving tokens such as USDT.[1]

items.title: Tron activates post-quantum cryptography on testnet
items.summary: Tron reportedly activated post-quantum cryptography on its testnet and said the upgrade could later move to mainnet.[3]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Tech firms pursue AI systems that improve themselves
items.summary: Technology companies and startups are increasingly automating machine-learning research, aiming to build AI systems that can design and train improved successors. The approach, known as recursive self-improvement, is also being explored for chip design, drug development, energy economics and cybersecurity.

items.title: Google opens advanced AI models to European researchers
items.summary: Google announced that 200 European researchers will receive access to its latest AI models, expanding research access to advanced systems.

items.title: Microsoft unveils local AI coding model and agent security tools
items.summary: Microsoft introduced an AI coding model designed to run directly on personal computers, alongside technology intended to stop AI agents from accessing data without authorization.

items.title: AI regulation and safety concerns intensify
items.summary: Microsoft President Brad Smith called for urgent global AI regulation and independent evaluators, while Yoshua Bengio warned that humanity is losing control of the technology. The developments reflect growing concern about safety standards for increasingly capable models.

items.title: AI-driven chip demand strains ASML capacity
items.summary: ASML said demand for chip-making equipment driven by AI is strong enough that it may not fully meet customer demand in 2027 and 2028, prompting the company to consider capacity expansion.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Nvidia updates DLSS 5 neural rendering
items.summary: Nvidia announced an updated DLSS 5 model that reportedly doubles performance versus its September version, cuts GPU overhead in half, and reduces 4K VRAM usage by 20%. The update is scheduled to debut October 16 in NBA 2K27, with Hogwarts Legacy and Yanyun Sixteen Sounds to follow.

items.title: Bloomberg details the making of Grand Theft Auto VI
items.summary: A Bloomberg feature examined Rockstar’s development of Grand Theft Auto VI, which is scheduled for release on November 19. The game is expected to be one of the largest entertainment launches ever, following record-breaking attention for its trailers and gameplay reveals.

items.title: Xbox launches Xbox Labs initiative
items.summary: Microsoft announced Xbox Labs, an initiative focused on emerging technologies, cross-platform adaptation, and artificial intelligence in game development. The program comes after management changes, layoffs, and restructuring across Xbox.

items.title: U.S. game spending reportedly fell 9% in August
items.summary: Circana data cited by The Fly indicated that U.S. video game spending declined 9% in August. NBA 2K27 led full-game dollar sales, while six new releases entered the month’s top ten best-selling games.

items.title: New esports arena opens in Sunderland
items.summary: A 15,000-square-foot esports arena opened in Sunderland alongside the National Esports Performance Campus. The venue is designed for live competitions, player training, and industry education, and includes a 200-seat theater and a large LED screen.

items.title: G-STAR faces major participation and timing challenges
items.summary: South Korea’s G-STAR game exhibition is reportedly facing reduced participation from major domestic publishers and competition from Grand Theft Auto VI’s November 19 release. Chinese companies are expected to provide some international representation.
